habitat: Grassland, vleis and thickets, usually but not necessarily near water. It will visit rain puddles on roads and flushes easily.
summary: An uncommon summer visitor. Heavily mottled upper parts and boldly barred underparts. The bill is pinkish, the eye is red, and there is often a narrow white eyebrow. The rump is mottled. Newman’s page uses the scientific name Crex egregia. This list keeps Crecopsis egregia. The call is a high-pitched chittering trill of eight or nine notes. Newman does not name the months, so they are unset. The Kemp name African Crake and the code VB were left unchanged.

similar.note: African Rail has a long red bill. African Crake has a shorter pinkish bill, a red eye and boldly barred underparts.
